message.content:
**C♯ Major Scale**

The C♯ major scale follows the standard major‑scale pattern of whole–whole–half–whole–whole–whole–half steps (W‑W‑H‑W‑W‑W‑H).  
Starting on C♯, the notes are:

| Step | Note |
|------|------|
| 1    | C♯ |
| 2    | D♯ |
| 3    | E♯ (enharmonically F) |
| 4    | F♯ |
| 5    | G♯ |
| 6    | A♯ |
| 7    | B♯ (enharmonically C) |
| 8    | C♯ (octave) |

So the full C♯ major scale is:

**C♯ – D♯ – E♯ – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – B♯ – C♯**

(If you prefer enharmonic equivalents, you can write it as C♯ – D♯ – E – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – B – C♯.)
